mcq.question: Why is `year_month_day{2026y, February, 30d}.ok()` false?

options.A: Because days above 28 are never allowed
options.B: February 2026 has only 28 days, and `ok()` checks the day against the real month length

mcq.explanation: C++20 calendar types can hold any field values, and `ok()` reports whether they form a real date, including leap-year rules.

mcq.question: An order arrives on Friday after the cut-off. With no holidays, on which day does it ship?
mcq.explanation: After the cut-off the order moves to the next day, and weekends are skipped, so the next business day after Friday is Monday.

bonus.question: Fixed UTC offsets ignore daylight saving time. When is that acceptable, and what does the C++20 time-zone database (`std::chrono::zoned_time`) add?
Write a failing test for `business_days_between(a, b, holidays)`, then implement it and check it against `add_business_days` for several pairs of dates.
